newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO Officials - U.S. attacks on Iraq unjustified.
newsitem.headline: PLO Officials - U.S. attacks on Iraq unjustified.

text.p: PLO officials on Tuesday denounced U.S. missile strikes on Iraq as unjustified and said Baghdad was entitled to protect its borders.
"We are against the U.S. attacks on Iraq. It is unjustified since it will create tension in the region," said Azzam al-Ahmad, the Palestine Liberation Organization's Ambassador to Iraq.

"Iraq's attacks against the Kurds in north of Iraq were an attempt to defend its national borders and to maintain the unity of the country. The international community, including the U.S., don't want Iraq's fragmentation," he told Reuters.
"Why is the U.S. allowing Turkish and Iranian armies to move against the Kurds, but when Iraq intervenes to protect its borders, it is bombed?" Ahmad said.
Ahmad, who is also a lawmaker in the Palestinian self-rule legislature, divides his time between Baghdad and Ramallah in the West Bank.
Palestinian Justice Minister Freih Abu Medein told Reuters: "The U.S. military adventure policy is not effective anymore."

The United States on Tuesday launched cruise missile attacks against air defence and communications targets in southern Iraq in retaliation for Iraqi military incursions into the Kurdish north on behalf of one of the two warring Kurdish factions.
The PLO angered the U.S. and its Western and Arab allies during the 1990-1991 Gulf crisis when it backed Iraqi President Saddam Hussein's invasion of Kuwait.
Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza ardently supported Hussein for launching Scud missile attacks on Israel while battling U.S.-led forces during the 1991 Gulf war.
But oil-rich Arab Gulf states severed relations with the PLO and halted financial aid to the organisation over its pro-Iraq stance. Palestinians working in some Gulf states were expelled.
